title: The Dungeon Dive Collection - 2019
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MsxCeW9nTb0

The second instalment of what Daniel (@dungeondive) here decides to make an annual tradition: a January walk of the shelves, noting what arrived and what left. Year two of the channel closed at around 550 subscribers, and the stated goal for 2019 is consistency — a video a week — plus long series on Myth ("a flawed gem", "very misunderstood") and possibly Shadows of Brimstone.

The departures carry the sharpest writing. Arcadia Quest goes because it is competitive and best at four players, and he wants games he can set up and play alone at any hour. Dungeon Saga goes because he hates it, and earns the video's best analogy: it's the long-awaited cult film finally arriving on DVD with "special features: English language, interactive menus." His specific complaint is that loot is divvied up between chapters and every in-play chest holds potions — which, for a dungeon crawl, removes the point.

The shelf tour is a period snapshot: Warhammer Quest, Kingdom Death, Secrets of the Lost Tomb named his favourite game, Hellboy and Blackstone Fortress yet to come. He closes on a practical worry that recurs for years afterward — game boxes are an impractical way to store a growing collection in a very small room.

----

Does an annual collection video work better as a record of what you kept, or of what you finally admitted you'd never play?
